Resolve Benchmark Controls

Source: R/04g-BenchMemoryConfig.R
BenchMemoryConfigSet.Rd

Merges the user supplied bench_config with the defaults and validates the names, so that a typo aborts instead of being silently ignored.

Usage

BenchMemoryConfigSet(
  rounds = 3L,
  probe_resources = TRUE,
  min_iterations = 1L,
  max_iterations = 1L,
  order = c("random", "fixed"),
  seed = getFuncOption("seed"),
  memory = TRUE,
  filter_gc = FALSE,
  check = FALSE,
  measure_rss = FALSE,
  on_failure = c("skip", "stop"),
  set_threads = 1L,
  min_time = 0.5,
  relative = FALSE,
  time_unit = NULL,
  timeout_sec = 10800L,
  ...
)

Arguments

rounds

integer. Number of benchmark rounds; every method is screened once per round and per-method summaries are taken across rounds. Odd values let the median ignore a single cold round. Must be at least 1. Default: 3L.

probe_resources

logical. Whether BenchMemory() should call bench_probe_resources() before staging the inputs. The probe calls gc() and can be expensive on large workspaces; disable it when the machine resource summary is not needed. Default: TRUE.

min_iterations

Each expression will be evaluated a minimum of min_iterations times.

max_iterations

Each expression will be evaluated a maximum of max_iterations times.

order

character. Order in which methods run within a round: "random" shuffles them (seeded by seed) to spread cold-cache and package-caching effects; "fixed" keeps the given method order. Default: c("random", "fixed") (first value used).

seed

integer. Base seed for shuffling method order each round; the round number is added to it. Also set inside each measurement child process. Default: 123L.

memory

If TRUE (the default when R is compiled with memory profiling), track memory allocations using utils::Rprofmem(). If FALSE disable memory tracking.

filter_gc

If TRUE remove iterations that contained at least one garbage collection before summarizing. If TRUE but an expression had a garbage collection in every iteration, filtering is disabled, with a warning.

check

Check if results are consistent. If TRUE, checking is done with all.equal(), if FALSE checking is disabled and results are not stored. If check is a function that function will be called with each pair of results to determine consistency.

measure_rss

logical. Whether to record peak process resident set size (RSS) in addition to R heap memory. Supported on Linux only. Default: FALSE.

on_failure

character. Action when a method times out or errors in a round: "skip" warns and continues with the remaining methods, "stop" aborts the whole benchmark. Default: c("skip", "stop") (first value used).

set_threads

integer. Number of threads the measurement child process is pinned to via SetThreads(), so runs stay comparable across methods. Default: 1L.

min_time

The minimum number of seconds to run each expression, set to Inf to always run max_iterations times instead.

relative

If TRUE all summaries are computed relative to the minimum execution time rather than absolute time.

time_unit

If NULL the times are reported in a human readable fashion depending on each value. If one of 'ns', 'us', 'ms', 's', 'm', 'h', 'd', 'w' the time units are instead expressed as nanoseconds, microseconds, milliseconds, seconds, hours, minutes, days or weeks respectively.

timeout_sec

numeric. Maximum wall-clock seconds allowed for one method in one round; the child process is killed when the limit is exceeded. Use Inf to disable the limit. Default: 10800L (3 hours).

...

Expressions to benchmark, if named the expression column will be the name, otherwise it will be the deparsed expression.

Value

A named list of resolved controls.

See also

Other ConfigSet: BenchGSEAConfigSet(), BenchGeneScoreConfigSet(), MethodParamSet()

Examples

# \donttest{
BenchMemoryConfigSet()
#> $rounds
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $probe_resources
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $min_iterations
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $max_iterations
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $order
#> [1] "random"
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 123
#> 
#> $memory
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $filter_gc
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $check
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $measure_rss
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $on_failure
#> [1] "skip"
#> 
#> $set_threads
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $min_time
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $relative
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $time_unit
#> NULL
#> 
#> $timeout_sec
#> [1] 10800
#> 
# }
